narration: Here's the trick. Each DNA letter stores two bits. Say A means zero zero, C means zero one, G means one zero, and T means one one. Take six bits, like zero one one zero one one. Split them into pairs. Zero one becomes C. One zero becomes G. One one becomes T. So those six bits become just C G T. Then a machine builds that exact strand, letter by letter. To read it back, another machine reads the letters and turns them back into bits.
description: Vertical 1080x1920 dark background, middle band focus. Top-middle: four mapping cards in a row A=00 in good=green, C=01 in accent=cyan, G=10 in accent2=magenta, T=11 in accent3=yellow, fg=white text. Center: six white bit tiles 0 1 1 0 1 1 in a row. Bottom-middle: horizontal strand slot, grey printer head block above it and cyan scanner light bar. All 2D flat motion graphics.
